# AgbofaTech Academy — Project Handover

**Status:** Feature-complete, deployment-ready. Not yet launched with live
payment keys.

**Last updated:** 27 July 2026

This document is the reference for anyone taking over the codebase. It records
what exists, how it fits together, what was verified, and — as honestly as
possible — what is still missing.

> Companion document: **`DEPLOYMENT.md`** is the step-by-step guide to getting
> this into production. **`AUTH_SETUP.md`** is the running build log, with the
> reasoning behind each phase's decisions.

---

## Table of contents

1. [Project overview](#1-project-overview)
2. [Tech stack](#2-tech-stack)

## 1. Project overview

**AgbofaTech Academy** is a digital education and e-commerce platform for the
Ghanaian market. It sells and delivers:

- **Courses** — video lessons, progress tracking, quizzes, certificates
- **Software licences** — instant key delivery (Microsoft, AI tools, etc.)
- **Bundles** — several products at a discount
- **Subscriptions** — recurring access
- **Live classes** — Google Meet / YouTube Live / Zoom, with attendance
- **Community** — per-course discussion forums

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Domain** | `agbofatech.com` |
| **Hosting** | Vercel (region `fra1`) |
| **Currency** | GHS (Ghana Cedi) |
| **Locale** | `en-GH`, timezone `Africa/Accra` |
| **Repository** | *(set on first push — see `DEPLOYMENT.md` Part 8)* |

### Design language

Dark cinematic theme. Background `#0A0A0A`, cards `#0F172A`, gold accent
`#D4AF37`, blue `#3B82F6`, text `#F8FAFC`, muted `#94A3B8`, success `#10B981`,
error `#EF4444`. Glassmorphism panels, Playfair Display headings, Inter body.

---

## 2. Tech stack

| Layer | Technology | Version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Framework | Next.js (App Router) | `15.5.22` |
| Language | TypeScript | `^5` (strict) |
| UI | React | `^19.0.0` |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS | `^3.4.17` |
| Animation | Framer Motion | `^12.42.2` |
| Database / Auth / Storage | Supabase | `@supabase/supabase-js ^2.110.8`, `@supabase/ssr ^0.12.3` |
| Payments | Paystack | `@paystack/inline-js ^2.22.2` |
| Email | Resend | `^6.18.0` |
| PDF (certificates) | `@react-pdf/renderer` | `^4.5.1` |
| Validation | Zod | `^4.4.3` |
| Toasts | Sonner | `^2.0.7` |
| PWA | `next-pwa` (Workbox) | `^5.6.0` + `@types/next-pwa ^5.6.9` |
| Runtime | Node.js | 20+ (22 recommended) |
| Database engine | PostgreSQL | 17 (Supabase-managed) |

**No external UI component library.** Every component is hand-built with
Tailwind — see `components/admin/ui.tsx` for the shared primitives (Button,
Card, Modal, Input, Select, Textarea, StatusPill, TableWrap, EmptyState…).

### Codebase size

- **89** API route handlers
- **57** pages
- **14** SQL migrations
- **34** tables with RLS enabled
- **95** RLS policies
- **47** `SECURITY DEFINER` database functions

---

## 3. Architecture

```
                            ┌─────────────────────────┐
                            │        Browser          │
                            │  React 19 · PWA · SW    │
                            └────────────┬────────────┘
                                         │ HTTPS
                            ┌────────────▼────────────┐
                            │         VERCEL          │
                            │  Next.js 15 App Router  │
                            │  · Server Components    │
                            │  · 89 API routes        │
                            │  · Middleware (authz)   │
                            │  · 2 Cron jobs          │
                            │  Region: fra1           │
                            └───┬────┬────┬────┬──────┘
                                │    │    │    │
          ┌─────────────────────┘    │    │    └──────────────────┐
          │                          │    │                       │
┌─────────▼─────────┐   ┌────────────▼┐  ┌▼──────────┐  ┌─────────▼────────┐
│     SUPABASE      │   │  PAYSTACK   │  │  RESEND   │  │  GOOGLE DRIVE    │
│                   │   │             │  │           │  │                  │
│ PostgreSQL 17     │   │ Inline      │  │ 9 email   │  │ Lesson video     │
│  34 RLS tables    │   │  checkout   │  │ templates │  │  (public links,  │
│  95 policies      │   │ Webhook →   │  │ HMAC      │  │   iframe embed)  │
│  47 SECDEF fns    │   │  /api/      │  │  unsub    │  │                  │
│ Auth (email)      │   │  webhook/   │  │  tokens   │  │ Not cacheable    │
│ Storage:          │   │  paystack   │  │           │  │  offline         │
│  public-media ✅  │   │ HMAC-SHA512 │  └───────────┘  └──────────────────┘
│  certificates 🔒  │   └─────────────┘
└───────────────────┘
```

### Request patterns

- **Server Components** query Supabase directly via `utils/supabase/server.ts`
  (cookie-scoped, RLS-enforced). This is the default.
- **Client Components** call `/api/*` routes, which re-check authorization
  server-side. Nothing trusts the client.
- **Privileged operations** (webhook fulfilment, certificate generation, all
  email, both crons) use `utils/supabase/admin.ts` — the service-role client,
  which **bypasses RLS**. Confined to trusted server contexts only.

### Key directories

```
app/
  (site)/          Public marketing pages, catalog, blog, shop
  dashboard/       Student area — courses, player, quizzes, products, forum
  instructor/      Instructor area — courses, students, grades, live, earnings
  admin/           Admin panel — 14 sections
  api/             89 route handlers
  actions/         Server actions (auth forms)
lib/
  queries/         Server-side data access, one module per domain
  validations/     Zod schemas
  admin/ instructor/ quiz/ live/ forum/ email/ ecommerce/ certificates/ pwa/
components/
  admin/ courses/ dashboard/ forum/ live/ products/ quiz/ pwa/ site/ ui/
supabase/
  migrations/      14 SQL files, applied in filename order
  seed.sql         Optional demo data
  production-check.sql  Post-deploy health report
utils/supabase/    server / client / middleware / admin clients
```

## 4. Database schema — the 14 migrations

Migrations are applied **in filename order**; each depends on the last. All are
**idempotent** and safe to re-run.

> **Note on naming:** the file numbers reflect actual build order, which
> diverged from the order features were requested. Several prompts asked for a
> number that was already taken; renaming would have broken dependency order, so
> the next free number was used and the divergence documented in
> `AUTH_SETUP.md`.

| # | File | Description | Main tables / objects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `…0001_profiles_and_handle_new_user.sql` | Identity foundation. Role enum, auto-profile trigger, role-escalation guard. | `profiles`, `user_role` enum, `is_admin()`, `handle_new_user()`, `prevent_role_escalation()`, `touch_updated_at()` |
| 2 | `…0002_catalog.sql` | Course catalog. | `categories`, `courses`, `lessons` |
| 3 | `…0003_dashboard.sql` | Student progress. Replaced `enrollments` with `purchases`. | `purchases`, `lesson_progress`, `recalc_course_progress()` |
| 4 | `…0004_payments.sql` | Orders and coupons. | `orders`, `coupons`, `fulfil_order()` |
| 5 | `…0005_admin.sql` | Admin CMS + public storage bucket. | `announcements`, `reviews`, `blog_posts`, `settings`, `contacts`, `public-media` bucket, `admin_stats()` |
| 6 | `…0006_certificates.sql` | Certificate issuance, private bucket. | `certificates`, `certificates` bucket, `is_course_complete()` |
| 7 | `…0007_instructor_role.sql` | Instructor role and invitations. | `instructor_invitations`, `profiles.bio/website/twitter`, `courses.instructor_id`, `owns_course()`, `is_instructor()`, `redeem_instructor_invitation()`, `instructor_stats()` |
| 8 | `…0008_quizzes.sql` | Quiz engine with server-side grading. | `quizzes`, `quiz_questions`, `quiz_options`, `quiz_attempts`, `quiz_responses`, `get_quiz_for_student()`, `start_quiz_attempt()`, `submit_quiz_attempt()`, `get_attempt_review()` |
| 9 | `…0009_quiz_anticheat.sql` | Proctoring: violations, timer, auto-void. | `quiz_attempts.violations/auto_submitted`, `quizzes.time_limit_minutes`, `record_quiz_violation()`, `quiz_violation_limit()` |
| 10 | `…0010_instructor_helpers.sql` | Single-arg helper overloads + instructor gradebook. | `is_instructor_of_course()`, `can_manage_quiz(uuid)`, `is_admin()`, `instructor_grades()` |
| 11 | `…0011_email_automation.sql` | Email templates, send log, preferences. | `email_templates`, `email_logs`, `email_preferences`, `abandoned_cart_candidates()`, `ensure_email_preferences()` |
| 12 | `…0012_advanced_ecommerce.sql` | Unified product catalog: software, bundles, subscriptions. | `products`, `software_keys`, `bundle_items`, `subscription_plans`, `user_subscriptions`, `claim_software_key()`, rewritten `fulfil_order()` |
| 13 | `…0013_live_classes.sql` | Live sessions and attendance. | `live_sessions`, `live_session_attendees`, `record_session_attendance()`, `live_reminder_candidates()`, `live_session_state()` |
| 14 | `…0014_discussion_forum.sql` | Per-course forums with moderation. | `forum_boards`, `forum_threads`, `forum_posts`, `forum_notifications`, `forum_reply()`, `forum_mark_solution()`, `forum_delete_post()` |

### Corrections to the original brief

Two items in the handover request do not match the codebase:

- **There is no analytics / audit-log migration.** Admin statistics come from
  `admin_stats()` and `instructor_stats()` (migrations 5 and 7), computed on
  read. No `audit_logs` table exists.
- **PWA has no migration.** It is entirely client + build configuration
  (`next.config.ts`, `public/manifest.json`, `public/offline.html`,
  `components/pwa/*`). No database objects.

### Money representation

**All money is `numeric(10,2)` in GHS major units** — `courses.price`,
`products.price`, `orders.amount`, `purchases.amount`,
`subscription_plans.price`, `coupons.discount_value`.

Conversion to pesewas happens **once**, at the Paystack boundary, via
`toMinorUnits()` in `lib/payments.ts`. The original spec for migration 12 asked
for integer pesewas; that was deliberately declined, because two money
representations in one checkout is how a 100× pricing bug ships.

---

## 5. Feature summary

### 5.1 Authentication

**What it does.** Email/password sign-up with mandatory confirmation, login,
password reset, role-based routing.

**Flows.** Register → confirmation email → click link → `/auth/callback`
exchanges the code for a session → welcome email fires → redirect by role
(`admin` → `/admin`, `instructor` → `/instructor`, else `/dashboard`).

**Tables.** `auth.users`, `profiles`.
**External.** Supabase Auth (email delivery for confirm/reset).
**Verified.** Full register→confirm→login→reset cycle; middleware gating; the
role-escalation trigger proved live against real PostgreSQL (a student
self-promoting to admin stays a student).

---

### 5.2 Course catalog & player

**What it does.** Public catalog with search and category filters; a purchased-
course player with Google Drive video, progress tracking and sequential locking.

**Flows.** Browse `/courses` → course page → enroll → `/dashboard/courses/[id]`
→ watch → Mark Complete → progress recalculates → 100% issues a certificate.

**Tables.** `categories`, `courses`, `lessons`, `purchases`, `lesson_progress`.
**External.** Google Drive (video iframe).
**Verified.** Catalog rendering, optimistic Mark Complete, sequential locking,
`forbidden()` returning a real 403 for unpurchased courses.

---

### 5.3 Payments & orders

**What it does.** Paystack inline checkout with coupon support, HMAC-verified
webhook fulfilment.

**Flows.** Checkout modal → `POST /api/orders` (price recomputed server-side) →
Paystack modal → success → webhook fulfils → access granted. A
`/api/orders/verify` fallback runs on redirect because Paystack cannot reach
localhost, and in production the redirect often beats the webhook.

**Tables.** `orders`, `purchases`, `coupons`.
**External.** Paystack.
**Verified.** Score/price injection ignored (server recomputes); webhook HMAC
5/5 (no sig 401, wrong sig 401, valid 200, replay → `alreadyProcessed`, tampered
body 401); coupon `used_count` incremented exactly once across a replay.

---

### 5.4 Quizzes & anti-cheat

**What it does.** Multiple-choice / true-false / short-answer quizzes, graded
entirely server-side, with a browser proctor.

**Flows.** Lesson → Take Quiz → fullscreen gate → one question at a time →
submit → server grades → pass auto-completes the lesson (and issues a
certificate if it is the final lesson).

**Tables.** `quizzes`, `quiz_questions`, `quiz_options`, `quiz_attempts`,
`quiz_responses`.
**Verified.** See [§9](#9-quiz-security) — this is the most heavily tested area.

---

### 5.5 Certificates

**What it does.** Generates an A4 PDF certificate on course completion, stored
privately and served through signed URLs.

**Flows.** Course hits 100% → `issueCertificate()` renders the PDF → uploads to
the private `certificates` bucket → returns a **7-day signed URL**. Admins can
issue manually with `force`.

**Tables.** `certificates`. **Bucket.** `certificates` (private).
**External.** `@react-pdf/renderer`.
**Verified.** PDF rendered and visually inspected — which caught a hyphenation
bug turning "ACADEMY" into "ACAD-EMY", fixed with
`Font.registerHyphenationCallback`.

> **Deliberate deviation:** the spec implied a public bucket. It is private.
> Certificates carry students' real names; a public bucket allows path
> enumeration and bulk harvesting.

---

### 5.6 Instructor role

**What it does.** A third role that can manage only its own courses — lessons,
quizzes, grades, students, reviews, earnings, live classes, forums.

**Flows.** Admin invites by email → single-use signed link →
`/register/instructor?token=` → account created → `POST /api/instructor/activate`
redeems the token and promotes the role.

**Tables.** `instructor_invitations`, `profiles.role`, `courses.instructor_id`.
**Verified.** 8/8 cross-tenant attacks blocked. `WITH CHECK` pins
`instructor_id = auth.uid()` so an instructor cannot reassign a course. No
client SELECT policy on `instructor_invitations`, so tokens are unenumerable.

> Cross-tenant reads frequently return **404 rather than 403** — RLS hides the
> row entirely, so the API cannot confirm it exists. This is stronger: no
> existence leak.

---

### 5.7 Advanced e-commerce

**What it does.** A unified `products` catalog covering courses, software
licences, bundles and subscriptions.

**Flows.**
- *Software*: buy → webhook claims a key atomically → key shown in
  `/dashboard/products` **and** emailed.
- *Bundle*: one payment → a `purchases` row per included item.
- *Subscription*: plan picker → Paystack → `user_subscriptions` row → cancel
  stops future charges (Paystack disabled **first**, then the local row).

**Tables.** `products`, `software_keys`, `bundle_items`, `subscription_plans`,
`user_subscriptions`, `orders`, `purchases`.
**External.** Paystack, Resend.
**Verified.** **No double-sell** under concurrency — `claim_software_key()` uses
`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; two buyers + two replayed webhooks fired simultaneously
produced exactly 2 sold keys, *different* keys, one per buyer. Three buyers
racing for one key produced exactly one sale and a logged shortfall.

> Out-of-stock is refused **before** payment (409). If a key still cannot be
> allocated at fulfilment, the order completes, the shortfall is logged loudly,
> and the webhook response carries `outOfStock` so an operator can intervene —
> rather than the customer discovering it.

---

### 5.8 Email automation

**What it does.** Nine templates fired by platform events, with per-user
preferences and one-click unsubscribe. See [§8](#8-email-automation).

**Tables.** `email_templates`, `email_logs`, `email_preferences`.
**External.** Resend.
**Verified.** 40/40 API assertions — internal-only auth, idempotency, marketing
opt-out honoured, provider failure logged without breaking the caller.

---

### 5.9 Live classes

**What it does.** Scheduled sessions on Google Meet / YouTube Live / Zoom, with
attendance tracking and automated reminders.

**Flows.** Instructor schedules → enrolled students emailed → reminder ~1h
before (cron every 10 min) → student clicks Join → attendance recorded → after
the session the instructor publishes a recording URL → students emailed once.

**Tables.** `live_sessions`, `live_session_attendees`.
**External.** Google Meet / YouTube / Zoom (links only — no API integration).
**Verified.** 14 live-PostgreSQL RLS assertions; non-enrolled students cannot
read `meeting_url` at all; students cannot fabricate attendance (no INSERT
policy — the RPC is the only path); reminder cron re-runs send nothing.

> **`live` status is derived, not stored** — computed from
> `start_at + duration` on read, so no cron exists merely to flip a flag and a
> student cannot fake a LIVE badge by changing their clock.

---

### 5.10 Discussion forum

**What it does.** One board per course, threads with one-level-nested replies,
solutions, moderation, in-app notifications and email.

**Flows.** Enrolled student opens the board → posts a thread → classmate
replies → author notified in-app + by email → author marks a reply as the
solution → gold badge, replier emailed. Instructors pin, lock and delete.

**Tables.** `forum_boards`, `forum_threads`, `forum_posts`,
`forum_notifications`.
**Verified.** 39 live-PostgreSQL assertions. Non-enrolled see zero rows;
`WITH CHECK` blocks posting as someone else; grandchild replies are re-parented
to depth 1; only one solution survives per thread; notifications cannot be
forged.

> **Posts are soft-deleted.** `parent_post_id` cascades, so hard-deleting a
> parent would silently destroy other people's replies.
> **Pin/lock is a column-level trigger**, because RLS grants row access but
> cannot restrict *which* columns change — without it, a thread author could pin
> their own thread.

---

## 6. Authentication & authorization

### Roles

| Role | Access |
| --- | --- |
| `student` | Own dashboard, purchased courses, quizzes, certificates, products, forums for enrolled courses |
| `instructor` | Everything a student has, plus `/instructor/*` scoped to **their own** courses |
| `admin` | Everything, including `/admin/*` |

Stored in `profiles.role` (`user_role` enum). Assigned `student` by default via
the `handle_new_user()` trigger.

### Three enforcement layers

Every protected operation is checked **three times**:

1. **Middleware** (`utils/supabase/middleware.ts`) — redirects unauthenticated
   users away from `/dashboard`, `/admin`, `/account`, `/instructor`; sends
   non-admins away from `/admin` and non-instructors away from `/instructor`.
   Admins may view the instructor area.
2. **API guards** — `requireAdmin()`, `requireInstructor()`,
   `requireQuizManager()`, `requireLiveManager()` plus per-resource
   `assert*Access()` helpers. 401 when signed out, 403 for the wrong role.
3. **Row Level Security** — 95 policies across 34 tables. The final authority.
   Even a bug in layers 1–2 cannot leak data past RLS.

### Role escalation is blocked at the database

`prevent_role_escalation()` is a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger on `profiles` that
silently reverts any `role` change not made by an admin. Verified live: a
student issuing `update profiles set role='admin' where id=<self>` remains a
student.

---

## 7. Payment flow

### One-time purchase

```
1. Student clicks Enroll / Buy now
2. POST /api/orders            (courses)
   POST /api/orders/product    (products, bundles, subscriptions)
     → server looks up the price IN THE DATABASE
     → validates any coupon
     → refuses if already owned (409) or out of stock (409)
     → creates a `pending` order with a unique payment_reference
     → returns amountMinor (pesewas) for Paystack
3. Paystack inline modal opens with that reference
4. On success, two independent paths race — both idempotent:
   a) Paystack POSTs /api/webhook/paystack   ← authoritative
   b) The browser calls /api/orders/verify   ← fallback for redirect-first
5. Either path calls fulfil_order(reference, data):
     · locks the order row (FOR UPDATE)
     · returns already_processed=true if already paid  ← replay safe
     · marks it paid
     · grants access by product type
     · increments coupon used_count exactly once
6. deliverPurchase() emails licence keys (never throws)
```

### What `fulfil_order()` grants, by type

| Type | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Course (legacy `course_id`) | One `purchases` row |
| `course` product | One `purchases` row linked to both course and product |
| `software` / `digital` | `claim_software_key()` assigns a key atomically, plus a `purchases` row |
| `bundle` | One `purchases` row **per included item**, plus one for the bundle itself |
| Subscription | A `user_subscriptions` row set `active`. When the plan has a `paystack_plan_code`, the checkout passes `plan` to the inline SDK so Paystack bills every interval automatically. |

### Subscription lifecycle

| Paystack event | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `charge.success` (with plan) | Subscription created, `active` — first period charged |
| `subscription.create`, `invoice.create`, `invoice.update` | Extends `ends_at` |
| `subscription.disable`, `subscription.not_renew` | `cancelled` |
| `invoice.payment_failed` | `expired` |

Cancelling from the dashboard calls Paystack's disable endpoint **first**, and
only marks the local row cancelled if that succeeds — otherwise the customer
would see "cancelled" while still being charged.

### Security properties

- The client **never sends a price**. Tampering with the request body is
  ignored; the server recomputes from the database.
- The webhook verifies **HMAC-SHA512** of the raw body against
  `PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY`. Missing or wrong signature → 401.
- Fulfilment is **idempotent** — replays grant nothing twice.

---

## 8. Email automation

Nine templates, all stored in `email_templates` and editable at `/admin/emails`
with a live preview and test-send.

| Template | Trigger event | Fired when | Type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `welcome` | `user.created` | Email **confirmed** (not at signup) | Transactional |
| `course_completed` | `course.completed` | Course reaches 100% | Transactional |
| `abandoned_cart` | `order.pending` | Order pending 24h+ (hourly cron) | **Marketing** |
| `software_delivery` | `product.purchased` | Licence key assigned | Transactional |
| `live_session_scheduled` | `live.session` | Instructor schedules a class | Transactional |
| `live_session_reminder` | `live.session` | ~1h before start (10-min cron) | Transactional |
| `live_session_recording` | `live.session` | Recording URL published | Transactional |
| `forum_thread_reply` | `forum.activity` | Someone replies to your thread | Transactional |
| `forum_solution_marked` | `forum.activity` | Your reply marked as solution | Transactional |

### Design decisions

- **The welcome email fires at confirmation, not signup.** At signup the
  address is unverified; mailing unverified addresses is how a sending domain
  gets burned by typos and spam traps.
- **Only `abandoned_cart` is marketing.** It respects
  `email_preferences.marketing_emails`. Everything else is transactional — a
  direct consequence of something the user did — and always sends. Suppressing
  those would mean silently withholding someone's certificate or licence key.
- **Templates sharing an event are selected by NAME**, not by event, so a
  reminder can never be sent in place of a recording notice.
- **Everything is idempotent.** One welcome per user; one completion mail per
  (user, course); one chase per order; one reminder per (session, student).
- **Unsubscribe works signed-out** via an HMAC-SHA256 token
  (`lib/email/tokens.ts`), constant-time compared. It only ever sets
  `marketing_emails = false`, so a leaked link is low-impact. Emails also carry
  `List-Unsubscribe` headers (a Gmail/Yahoo bulk-sender requirement).
- **Email failures never break the operation that triggered them.**
  `sendAutomatedEmail()` always resolves. A dead provider cannot roll back a
  purchase.
- **Admin test-sends are not logged**, so testing a template cannot suppress the
  real one.

---

## 9. Quiz security

The most adversarially tested part of the system.

### The answer key never reaches the browser

- **Students have no SELECT policy on `quiz_options`** — every row carries
  `is_correct`. A direct query returns **0 rows** for a student and 5 for the
  instructor. Verified.
- Students receive questions only through `get_quiz_for_student()`
  (`SECURITY DEFINER`), which builds the JSON explicitly and **omits**
  `is_correct` and `model_answer`.
- The answer key is revealed only *after* submission, by
  `get_attempt_review()`, which refuses while `completed_at is null`.

### Grading is server-side and unforgeable

`submit_quiz_attempt()` receives only the student's *choices*. Sending
`{"score": 100}` yields a true 0%. Verified.

### Anti-cheat

The browser proctor (`lib/quiz/anticheat.ts`) enforces fullscreen, detects tab
switches (`visibilitychange` + `blur`), blocks devtools shortcuts, disables
copy/paste/right-click, and warns on unload.

**It is a deterrent, not a security boundary** — any of it can be disabled with
devtools. The rules that decide a grade live in SQL:

1. **Violations are monotonic.** `record_quiz_violation()` and
   `submit_quiz_attempt()` both take `MAX(incoming, stored)`. A tampered client
   sending `violations: 0` cannot clear what is already recorded.
2. **Reaching the limit (3) voids the attempt in SQL** — score 0, `passed`
   false, regardless of how correct the answers were.
3. **The timer is enforced against `started_at` and the database clock**
   (plus 30s skew grace), never the client countdown.
4. **`auto_submitted` is one-way.** The client can set it; only the server can
   decide it was not.
5. Refreshing mid-quiz **resumes** the same attempt — it does not reset the
   timer or wipe violations.

Verified: all-correct answers submitted at 3 violations score **0**; a
4-violation attempt claiming `violations: 0` is still voided.

## 10. PWA & offline support

Configured through `next-pwa` (Workbox) in `next.config.ts`.

### Caching strategies

| Content | Strategy | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/*` | **NetworkOnly** | Auth-scoped; a cache would leak one user's data to the next person on a shared device |
| Auth pages, `/unsubscribe` | **NetworkOnly** | Stale session state after sign-out |
| Supabase REST/Auth | **NetworkOnly** | RLS-scoped data |
| Live quiz routes | **NetworkOnly** | An attempt must never be replayed from cache |
| `/forum/*` | **NetworkOnly** | Threads change constantly |
| Paystack, Google Drive | **NetworkOnly** | Third-party, always live |
| Signed storage URLs | **NetworkOnly** | Private certificates |
| Google Fonts CSS | StaleWhileRevalidate | |
| Google Fonts files | CacheFirst (1yr) | |
| `/_next/static/*` | CacheFirst (1yr) | Content-hashed, immutable |
| Images, `/_next/image` | StaleWhileRevalidate | |
| Public Supabase storage | StaleWhileRevalidate | Thumbnails only |
| Page navigations | **NetworkFirst** (6s timeout) | Fresh online, cached offline |

### Install & offline

- `public/manifest.json` — standalone display, gold theme, 8 icons (including
  two maskable), 3 app shortcuts.
- `components/pwa/install-prompt.tsx` — captures `beforeinstallprompt`, shows a
  branded banner on mobile only, snoozes dismissal for 30 days in
  `localStorage`.
- `public/offline.html` — fully self-contained branded fallback (no external
  CSS, fonts or JS), served when a navigation fails with nothing cached.
- `components/pwa/offline-banner.tsx` — non-blocking top bar when offline.

### Two bugs worth knowing about

1. **`next-pwa` auto-registration silently does nothing on the App Router.** It
   injects into the `main.js` webpack entry, which is Pages-Router-only; the App
   Router builds `main-app.js`. `/sw.js` was generated and served, but nothing
   ever registered it. Fixed with an explicit `components/pwa/register-sw.tsx`.
2. **`next-pwa` precaches `app-build-manifest.json`, which Next 15 never
   serves.** The 404 rejected Workbox's install, so the entire service worker
   went redundant — while `/sw.js` still returned 200 and looked healthy.
   Diagnosed via CDP `ServiceWorker.workerErrorReported`; fixed by adding it to
   `buildExcludes`.

Both would have been invisible to an HTTP-status-only check.

## 11. Testing summary

No automated test suite is committed. Verification was performed
**per feature phase** against hand-written stateful stubs (emulating PostgREST,
GoTrue and the Resend API) and, for the last three phases, against **real
PostgreSQL 17** with RLS enforced as a genuine `authenticated` role.

### Totals by category

| Category | Assertions | What it covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **SQL / RLS (real PostgreSQL)** | ~90 | Live RLS as `authenticated`, trigger guards, cross-tenant isolation, all 14 migrations applied both file-by-file and in a single transaction |
| **API** | ~400 | Auth gating, tamper resistance, idempotency, concurrency, error codes |
| **Browser (Playwright)** | ~180 | Real rendering, screenshots inspected by eye, user flows end to end |
| **Non-regression** | ~150 | Re-run after every phase: prior pages, quiz security, PWA, payments |
| **Unit** | 13 | HMAC tokens, placeholder rendering |

### Highest-value results

- **Quiz:** raw student payload contains no `is_correct`/`model_answer`; direct
  `quiz_options` query as student → **0 rows**; `{"score":100}` → true 0%.
- **Payments:** HMAC 5/5; replay → `alreadyProcessed`; coupon counted once.
- **Concurrency:** two simultaneous webhooks → 2 *different* licence keys, never
  the same one twice. Three buyers, one key → exactly one sale.
- **Cross-tenant:** 8/8 instructor attacks blocked; forum and live-class
  outsiders see zero rows.
- **Live PostgreSQL** caught a bug no stub could: admins could not see live
  sessions, because a permissive `FOR ALL` policy does not satisfy a `SELECT`
  when a SELECT-specific policy also exists.

### Verification discipline

**HTTP 200 does not mean working.** Several bugs were found *only* by rendering
in a real browser and looking at the screenshot:

- PDF hyphenation ("ACAD-EMY")
- A modal clipped by a transformed ancestor (Framer Motion leaves `transform`,
  which becomes the containing block for `position: fixed`)
- An RSC error where curl returned 200 and the browser showed a blank page
  (functions cannot cross the Server/Client boundary)

### Known testing limitations

- **No live third-party transaction.** No real Paystack payment, no real email
  delivered to an inbox, no real Google Meet session hosted, no real Drive video
  played.
- **Recurring billing is stub-only.** See §13.
- **No CI.** Verification was manual per phase; there is no `npm test`.
- **No load testing.** Behaviour under concurrent real traffic is unknown.

Full table with example values and sources: `DEPLOYMENT.md` Part 10.

> **The build succeeds with zero environment variables and then 500s at
> runtime.** With only `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` missing the site looks
> healthy but every payment webhook fails — students are charged and get
> nothing. This is the single most important operational fact about the
> project.

### Deploying an update

```bash
git add . && git commit -m "..." && git push
```

Vercel builds `main` automatically; PRs get preview URLs. **If the change
includes a migration, apply it to production around the same time** — an app
expecting a column that does not exist will error.

### Security headers

`vercel.json` sets `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`,
`X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`,
a restrictive `Permissions-Policy`, and `Cache-Control: no-store` on `/api/*`.

## 13. Known issues & future work

### Blocking for a complete launch

1. **Recurring billing is wired but has never been tested against live
   Paystack.** `POST /api/orders/product` now returns `paystackPlanCode`, and
   `components/products/buy-button.tsx` passes it to the inline SDK as `plan`,
   which is what makes Paystack create a real subscription rather than a
   one-time charge. The webhook already handles `invoice.create`,
   `invoice.update`, `subscription.disable` and `invoice.payment_failed`.
   **Remaining work is verification, not code:** create a Plan in the Paystack
   dashboard, paste its `PLN_…` code into the plan's `paystack_plan_code` field
   in `/admin/products`, subscribe with a test card, then confirm in Paystack
   that a *subscription* was created and that
   `user_subscriptions.paystack_subscription_code` was populated by the webhook.
   A plan with no code configured still works — it charges one period and logs
   a console warning — so a misconfigured plan degrades visibly rather than
   silently.
2. **Vercel Hobby runs cron jobs once per day**, regardless of schedule. The
   1-hour live-class reminder is effectively useless on the free tier. Either
   upgrade to **Pro** (no code change needed) or drive the endpoints from an
   external scheduler — both options, with copy-pasteable configuration, are in
   `DEPLOYMENT.md` → *Vercel Cron on the Free Tier*.
3. **No live payment has ever been processed.** Complete the test-mode
   checklist, then do one real low-value purchase and refund it.

### Important but not blocking

4. **Email bounce and complaint handling is not wired.** The `email_logs.status`
   enum supports `bounced` and `complaint`, but nothing writes them. Add a
   Resend webhook so hard bounces auto-suppress; without it, repeated sends to
   dead addresses will damage domain reputation.
5. **Forum threads and posts are not paginated** — capped at 100 threads and 500
   posts per query. Needs cursor pagination before any board gets busy.
6. **The notification bell polls every 60s** rather than using Supabase
   Realtime. Fine now; laggy on an active board.
7. **Instructor invitation emails are not sent.** The admin copies the link
   manually. The UI states this explicitly. Wire it to the existing Resend
   pipeline.
8. **Live-class attendance records the join click only.** `left_at` and
   `duration_minutes` exist in the schema but nothing populates them — neither
   Meet nor Zoom reports departure without their server-side APIs.
9. **Google Meet links are pasted manually.** `createMeetLink()` can slot in
   behind the platform selector once Google Calendar OAuth is added.

### Nice to have

10. **No automated test suite / CI.** Verification was thorough but manual.
    Porting the phase scripts into Playwright + a SQL harness under GitHub
    Actions would protect against regressions.
11. **Rich text is plain text.** Admin content fields and forum posts are
    textareas rendered with `whitespace-pre-line`. TipTap or MDX would be an
    upgrade — but note that plain text is also why there is no XSS surface.
12. **`/verify` certificate page does not exist.** The generated PDF prints
    "Verify this certificate at agbofatech.com/verify". That route needs
    building, or the PDF text changing.
13. **Quiz drag-and-drop** is implemented as up/down buttons (the spec allowed
    either).
14. **No analytics dashboard beyond `admin_stats()`.** No audit log of
    administrative actions.
15. **Physical products are unsupported.** Deliberately omitted from the product
    type enum — shipping, stock and returns were unspecified.
